text: {"findings":[{"rule":"K2","where":"ClaimIssuer.getRecoveredAddress / ClaimIssuer.isClaimValid / ClaimIssuer.revokeClaim, reached via Identity.addClaim","severity":"HIGH","why":"Revocation is keyed on the exact signature bytes, but getRecoveredAddress does not reject high-s ECDSA signatures. A revoked claim's malleated twin (s replaced by n-s, v flipped) recovers to the same issuer signer, so isClaimValid returns true for it. The investor wallet can re-add that twin as its own claim, which makes the wallet KYC-verified again and lets it receive tokens.","steps":"1) Issuer admin calls claimIssuer.revokeClaim(claimId, idA) for investor a1. 2) a1 (management key on idA) calls idA.addClaim(1, 1, claimIssuer, malleatedSig, KYC-OK data, \"\") where malleatedSig = (r, n-s, v^1) of the revoked signature. The claim is accepted because isClaimValid passes on the twin. 3) Any sender calls token.transfer(a1, amount); isVerified(a1) is true and the transfer succeeds."},{"rule":"J2","where":"IdentityRegistry.updateCountry","severity":"HIGH","why":"updateCountry only emits CountryUpdated and never writes the country into IdentityRegistryStorage. The country module reads the stored country, so a wallet whose country is changed to 408 keeps its old country and can still receive tokens.","steps":"1) Agent calls ir.updateCountry(b, 408). The event is emitted but storage still holds 356 (INDIA) for b. 2) Sender calls token.transfer(b, amount). isVerified(b) is true, and CountryRestrictModule.moduleCheck reads investorCountry(b)=356, which is not restricted, so the transfer succeeds."}]}
